name: Maple Syrup Caramels

cookwares.name: candy thermometer or leave-in probe thermometer

instructions.primary_message: Line an 8-by 20-cm square baking pan with aluminum foil, leaving a 5-cm overhang on two sides. Line pan again with parchment paper, leaving overhang on alternate sides from foil. Lightly oil parchment or spray with nonstick cooking spray. Set aside.
Combine heavy cream, butter, sea salt, and maple extract (if using) in a small saucepan and bring to a boil. Immediately remove saucepan from heat and set aside.

Combine sugar, maple syrup, corn syrup, and water in a large saucepan. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves. Boil without stirring, swirling pan occasionally until mixture has gone from light to dark amber, about 6 minutes.

Carefully pour cream mixture into sugar mixture. It will bubble vigorously. Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer until a candy thermometer registers 120°C. Pour caramel into prepared pan. Allow caramel to cool for at least 3 hours. Cut caramel into 2.5-cm pieces using kitchen shears and wrap pieces in wax paper. Caramels will keep for at least a week stored in an airtight container at room temperature, and even longer in refrigerator.

schema_metadata.keywords: Edible DIY, holiday baking, maple, maple syrup

description: Flavored with plenty of pure maple syrup and just a hint of sea salt, these sensational (and seasonal!) caramels are simple to prepare and totally crave-worthy.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 3 hr 25 min.

Optional or for serving: 1/2 teaspoon maple extract (optional)
author: Lucy Baker
